subject.title: fix(agents): make model-facing tool schemas llama.cpp GBNF-compatible

question: Should llama.cpp compatibility use the existing centralized provider/model schema-cleaning seam, or should core tool schemas permanently omit these constraints for every provider?
rationale: The observed bug and proof are strong, but choosing whether model-facing schemas are globally structural-only or retain provider-supported semantic constraints defines a cross-provider compatibility contract that automation should not decide.

options.title: Centralize provider cleaning
options.body: Preserve the canonical tool schemas and strip `pattern` and excessive `maxLength` only for configured grammar-constrained backends through `applyProviderCleaning`.

options.title: Adopt structural-only schemas
options.body: Accept the global constraint removals, but explicitly establish this as core policy and add parity tests proving every removed rule remains enforced after tool dispatch.

recommendation.title: Centralize provider cleaning
recommendation.body: Preserve the canonical tool schemas and strip `pattern` and excessive `maxLength` only for configured grammar-constrained backends through `applyProviderCleaning`.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work most directly owns the cron model-schema and canonicalization boundary affected by this choice.
